parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Salvation and Grace. <short pause> I'm Sarah Mitchell. Tonight, we're asking a quiet question... <short pause> is there any place too far for God's grace to reach?

Maybe you've felt distant from God. <short pause> Maybe you've wondered if you've wandered too far, made too many wrong turns, or stayed away too long. <short pause> Let's turn to something the apostle Paul wrote to believers in Ephesus... words that shine light into that very fear.
But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ... <short pause> by grace ye are saved. <long pause>

Paul begins with two words... <short pause> but God. <short pause> Everything changes... with those two words. <short pause> Before this passage, Paul has painted a sobering picture of humanity's condition... dead in trespasses and sins, following the course of this world, living in the passions of the flesh. <short pause> It's a portrait of people utterly unable to save themselves... spiritually lifeless, cut off from the source of life.
But God. <short pause> Into that darkness... into that spiritual death... God moves.
Not because we deserved it. <short pause> Not because we earned it. <short pause> Not because we were good enough, or tried hard enough. <short pause> He moved because of his great love for us.
Notice what Paul says next. <short pause> God is rich in mercy.

parts.style: gently emphatic, a hint of wonder
parts.text: Not stingy with mercy. <short pause> Not carefully rationing it out. <short pause> RICH in mercy. <short pause> There's an abundance here... a lavishness... an ocean of mercy, deeper than any pit we could fall into.

And this mercy flows from love. <short pause> God's great love. <short pause> This isn't love as a feeling, or a sentiment. This is love as action... love that reaches down into our deadness, and does something about it.

parts.style: curious, rhetorical question, then a warm answer
parts.text: What does God do? <short pause> He makes us alive together with Christ.

The same power that raised Jesus from the grave... is the power at work in salvation. <short pause> God doesn't repair our old life. He doesn't improve what was broken. <short pause> He gives life... where there was death. <short pause> Paul adds a phrase in parentheses, as if he can't help but insert it... by grace, you have been saved. <short pause> He'll say it again at the end of the passage, but he says it here too... as if to make sure we don't miss it.
This is grace. <short pause> This is gift. <short pause> This is something done for us... not something we did for ourselves.

Then Paul goes further. <short pause> God raised us up with Christ, and seated us with him in the heavenly places. <short pause> This isn't just rescue from death. This is elevation... to a place of honor, of belonging, of closeness to God himself.

And why? <short pause> So that in the coming ages, God might show the immeasurable riches of his grace, in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. <short pause> God's purpose stretches beyond this moment... beyond this life... into ages yet to come. <short pause> His grace is so rich, so vast, that it takes eternity to display it fully.

Now, listen to how Paul summarizes it all. <short pause> For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God... <short pause> not of works, lest any man should boast. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: By grace. <short pause> Through faith. <short pause> Not of yourselves. <short pause> The gift of God. <short pause> Not of works.

Every phrase drives home the same truth... this is all from God. <short pause> Grace is the source. Faith is the means... and even that faith is a gift. <short pause> There's nothing in us that earns this... nothing we contribute to make it happen. <short pause> It's not of works, Paul says, lest anyone should boast. <short pause> If salvation came from our effort, we'd compare ourselves to each other. We'd wonder if we'd done enough. We'd boast in our achievements, or despair at our failures.
But grace silences all that. <short pause> Grace levels the ground. <short pause> Grace removes every reason to boast... and every reason to despair.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So where does this leave you tonight... as you lie here in the quiet? <short pause> If you've been carrying the weight of your failures, wondering if you've gone too far for God to reach you... <short pause> hear this. <short pause> God is rich in mercy. <short pause> His love moved toward you... when you were dead in your sins. <short pause> Distance doesn't limit his grace. Your past doesn't exhaust his mercy.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: If you've been striving, trying to earn your way to God, trying to be good enough... <exhales> here's rest. <short pause> It is the gift of God, not of works. <short pause> You can't add to what Christ has done. You can't improve on grace. <short pause> You can only receive it.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And if you've already trusted in Jesus... let these words settle deep tonight. <short pause> You are alive in Christ. <short pause> You are seated with him. <short pause> You are loved... with a great love. <short pause> Not because of what you did today, or didn't do. <short pause> Because of what God has done.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, thank you that your grace reaches as far as we could ever wander... and deeper than we could ever fall. <short pause> Help us rest tonight in the finished work of Jesus... trusting not in ourselves, but in your great love.
Goodnight. <short pause> And may the peace of Christ be with you.
